commits.message:
feat(reporting): add admin dashboard, natural-language assistant, and daily digest

Three pieces, all built on the same shared, read-only data layer
(app/reporting/service.py) so a number on the dashboard, the answer to
the same question asked in chat, and the morning Telegram digest can
never disagree with each other:

1. app/reporting/service.py -- taxonomy size/growth (7d/30d, from
   taxonomy_candidates.reviewed_at), candidate queue health (pending
   count + oldest-pending age per signal type), daily triage activity
   (approved/rejected, split automated vs human reviewer), LLM cost
   trend (live from the self-hosted Langfuse Daily Metrics API -- see
   the User-Agent workaround for a Cloudflare 403 in front of it), and
   parsing quality (draft volume, avg confidence, % needing review).
   New GET /reports/overview (+ narrower per-section endpoints) in
   app/routers/reporting.py.

   Caught and fixed a real bug while building this: get_candidate_
   queue_health originally counted raw taxonomy_candidates rows, which
   reported "37,362 pending boilerplate lines" -- record_boilerplate_
   line_candidates deliberately writes a row for every distinct line
   seen (most from one company's own one-off content), and only ever
   surfaces one for review once it's crossed 8+ distinct sender
   domains (see app/understanding/taxonomy/candidates.py). The real
   reviewable count was 6. Fixed to apply the same distinct_senders
   filter list_taxonomy_candidates already does; covered by a
   regression test so this can't silently regress again.

2. app/assistant/service.py -- a natural-language question-answering
   endpoint (POST /assistant/query), deliberately NOT a text-to-SQL
   agent (an LLM with raw SQL access to production data is a real
   correctness risk -- a subtly wrong WHERE clause returns a subtly
   wrong number with total confidence). Instead: a fixed set of safe,
   read-only TOOLS -- the same 5 reporting functions above, plus a
   pending-candidate search -- the model can only ever pick one of and
   supply parameters for, never write its own query. Two LLM calls per
   question: pick a tool + params, then compose a plain-English answer
   from that tool's actual result. A tool-selection response that
   fails to parse falls back to a plain "couldn't find data for that"
   rather than guessing.

3. scripts/hermes-950-daily-telegram-digest.py -- a passive companion
   to the in-app dashboard, sent to the same Telegram channel already
   used for operational alerts, so the status shows up each morning
   without anyone needing to go look. Prints the digest and skips
   sending (rather than failing) when Telegram isn't configured for
   the run. Not yet wired to a systemd timer -- sending an unsolicited
   message needs the user's go-ahead first.

Frontend: two new pages under the same nav as the existing taxonomy/
moderation pages -- Reports (stat cards + lightweight inline-SVG bar
charts, no new chart-library dependency) and Assistant (a chat panel
with starter-question chips, keeps the last 8 turns as context for
follow-up questions).

New coverage in scripts/hermes-950-reporting-assistant-check.py (10
checks): every reporting function's response shape, the boilerplate-
threshold regression test above, graceful degradation without
Langfuse/LiteLLM configured, and both new endpoints via the real
FastAPI app. Verified end-to-end against real production data (not
just the test suite): a natural-language question about job-title
approvals and LLM cost this week correctly routed to the right tool
and produced an accurate, concrete answer. Full regression suite run
against a fresh schema and freshly built image: hermes-950-reporting-
assistant-check.py passes all 10 checks; every other failure in the
suite reproduces identically against the current, unmodified
production image in the same throwaway harness (missing live server,
missing Langfuse/MS Graph credentials) -- confirmed pre-existing
environment gaps, not regressions from this change. Frontend
type-checks and builds clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
